Q: How to dynamically set the sender email address in Resend for NextJS? A:

You can adjust the subject property at your resend function in the route.ts file by setting the subject value to ;

subject: `New Application from ${formData.get("email")} for ${formData.get("role")} Position`,

Q: Writing a SUBSTRING() call in CodeIgniter's select() method renders SQL with corrupted quotes A:

This appears to be a problem related to a version of CodeIgniter prior to version 3.

The protect_identifiers() method which is implemented for several query builder method, including select(), will implicitly disable automatic quoting in a SELECT condition if it contains a parenthesis or a single quote.

This means that your query will work as originally scripted in CI3.

It should be mentioned that it is generally suboptimal to save date values as a non-DATE type column in a database because it prevents direct access to helpful date functions.

Also, you can omit the from() call if you nominate the table name in your get() call.

Q: How to reset a CUDA GPU in python A:

Perhaps as a last resort you could use nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <ID> to reset specific processes associated with the GPU ID. In Jupyter notebook you should be able call it by using the os library. Nevertheless, the documentation of nvidia-smi states that the GPU reset is not guaranteed to work in all cases.

You may want to visit this other post before doing anything with this command-line tool: What does the command "nvidia-smi --gpu-reset" do?

Q: Converting existing project to Spring boot project in InelliJ A:

  1. In your maven pom.xml or build.gradle file, you can add the spring boot starter dependency:

    spring-boot-starter (the group id is org.springframework.boot)

  2. Open the project in Intellij and then right click on the project => Add Framework support => then you can select accordingly

Q: Python - Access Control Allow Origin A:

As e4c5 mentioned, you need to make a CORS request. Since the jquery isn't being served from the same server that is providing gen.py, you need a header on the python server side to allow the browser to retrieve the resource. This same-origin policy is to prevent cross-site scripting.

To do so with BaseHTTPServer, you're going to need to redefine the request handler and provide a call to self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*"). This answer shows how to do it with BaseHTTPServer, but it's fairly long and involved.

This answer has a pretty simple implementation of how to set the CORS header on SimpleHTTPServer, which has a similar structure to BaseHTTPServer which you can pretty easily port over.

*Regarding the * in the send_header call, this allows requests from any origin to get gen.py. Depending on what this is, it may not matter but you may want to set a more restrictive policy if it does.
